report: I went to the airport, the flight was delayed, and I reached late.
story: I had one job: reach Delhi by six for my cousin's sangeet. At the gate, the screen flashed: **Delayed, 4 hours.**
trick: start with what you wanted, then what got in the way

yourTurn.prompt: Tell today's commute in two lines.
yourTurn.hint: Line 1: what you wanted. Line 2: what got in the way.

report: I missed the bus and walked.
story: I reached the stop just as the bus pulled away. The driver gave me a cheerful wave. I walked the whole thirty minutes home.
trick: Put the reader at the moment things change.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a time you just missed something.
yourTurn.hint: Start at the moment you realised.

report: I cooked dinner and it was too spicy.
story: I wanted to impress my friends with dinner. One bite in, everyone reached for water at the same time.
trick: Show the reaction instead of naming the problem.

report: I lost my keys but found them.
story: I searched every pocket for my keys. Then my bag started jingling. They were in the one pocket I hadn't checked.
trick: Hold the answer until the last line.

yourTurn.hint: What did you check before finding it?

report: My first presentation went well.
story: My hands shook as I opened the slides. Then someone nodded at my first point. I finally remembered to breathe.
trick: Show a small sign that changed how you felt.

report: I got on the wrong train.
story: I settled into my seat, proud of being early. Then the announcement named a city in the opposite direction.
trick: Set up confidence before the surprise.

report: A stranger helped me with my bags.
story: I was facing three flights of stairs with two heavy bags. A stranger picked one up and said, 'Which floor?'
trick: Let one line of dialogue carry the kindness.

report: It rained and I got wet.
story: The forecast promised sunshine, so I left my umbrella. Ten minutes later, I was sharing a tiny shop doorway with six strangers.
trick: Use a concrete detail to make the scene visible.

yourTurn.hint: What did the weather make you do?

report: I finally ran five kilometres.
story: For weeks, I stopped at the same tea stall to catch my breath. Today I ran past it. I almost went back to celebrate.
trick: Show progress through one familiar landmark.

report: My colleague helped during a meeting.
story: The client asked for a number I couldn't find. Before the silence grew, Meera slid her notebook towards me. There it was.
trick: Build a little tension before the help arrives.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a moment someone helped you.

report: I taught my father to use video calls.
story: Dad finally joined the video call. For a full minute, all I could see was his ceiling. Then his smiling face appeared.
trick: Choose one moment rather than the whole process.

report: The cafe gave me the wrong drink.
story: I ordered coffee and took a confident sip. It was hot chocolate. For once, I decided a mistake could stay.
trick: End with your response to the surprise.

report: There was a power cut during dinner.
story: Halfway through dinner, the lights went out. We lit a candle. Without the TV, we ended up talking for an hour.
trick: Show how a small problem changed the evening.

report: My new shoes hurt my feet.
story: I wore new shoes to look sharp on my first day. By lunch, I was planning every trip around the nearest chair.
trick: Replace a general feeling with visible behaviour.

yourTurn.hint: What did you do because of it?

report: My plant started growing again.
story: I nearly threw the plant away. Then I spotted one tiny green leaf. Now it has the best place by the window.
trick: Make one small detail the turning point.

report: My friends surprised me on my birthday.
story: I thought everyone had forgotten my birthday. Then the doorbell rang, and someone outside whispered far too loudly, 'Hide the cake!'
trick: Use a sound to reveal the surprise.

yourTurn.hint: What did you hear or see first?

report: I found a good bakery nearby.
story: I took a wrong turn on my walk. The smell of fresh bread made me stop. Now I take that wrong turn every Sunday.
trick: Connect the accident to what changed afterwards.

report: I fixed a loose chair.
story: The chair had wobbled for months. I finally tightened one screw. Two minutes of work, and breakfast stopped feeling like a balancing act.
trick: Contrast the long annoyance with the small fix.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a small win at home.
yourTurn.hint: How long had you put it off?

report: I showed a new colleague around.
story: On my first day, I ate lunch alone. When the new colleague arrived, I pulled out the chair beside me.
trick: Link a past experience to a present choice.

report: I spoke up in a meeting.
story: I rehearsed my question silently three times. Then I raised my hand. Someone said, 'I was wondering that too.'
trick: End with the response that mattered.

yourTurn.prompt: Tell a time you spoke despite nerves.
yourTurn.hint: What happened after your first words?
